account:
Something unusually coordinated is being prepared for my six-o'clock appointment in the great hall today. Innkeeper requested the appointment yesterday, specifically asking secretary to escort me, and it is approved for eighteen to eighteen thirty under the broad subject of civic hospitality and community gatherings. Despite repeated questions, I have not received committee names or a detailed agenda. Secretary has spoken with innkeeper, builder, freight, and baker during preparations; innkeeper and builder say everything is ready. Neighbour heard that innkeeper, freight, and builder ordered refreshments. I also heard a townsfolk report that builder carried a sack of bread. A lantern appeared in the great hall yesterday, though I do not know whether that is connected.

The bread arrangements remain unclear: baker could not verify payment for the original order, and secretary says baker and freight are reconciling it to avoid charging twice. Innkeeper proposes no bridge or port changes and no treasury spending, according to secretary. I have asked that no treasury payment be authorized before reconciliation. There were no council letters waiting today.

My impression is that this is an organized social or civic occasion, possibly with an element being deliberately kept from me, rather than an ordinary policy meeting. Refreshments, preparations, and a precise escorted arrival suggest a reception or perhaps a surprise, but that is only speculation. I have no evidence of wrongdoing. Neighbour appears curious as well and has now come to ask whether visitors may listen; neither of us has obtained a clear answer about public access. I am still in my office with secretary and neighbour, shortly before the appointment, intending to attend and learn directly what the organizers have planned.
